# How often couplings act: settling, runaway and its rate

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`how-often-couplings-act` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](how-often-couplings-act.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> The most difference that can arrive is at most D·(1 + M)^a, a the steps where anything couples, attained by a self-loop; with natural-number strengths each return at least doubles it: frequent returns run away, rare couplings stay polynomial; every schedule settling is exactly Σ⁰₂ excluded middle.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. A schedule marks steps, and its count is the number of marked steps before t: it does not fall, rises by at most one a step and is at most t; where the count passes its value at N, a step from N on is marked, so a schedule with unbounded count marks steps as late as one likes. (`Becoming.Frequency.count`, `Becoming.Frequency.count_succ_on`, `Becoming.Frequency.count_succ_off`, `Becoming.Frequency.bif_le_one`, `Becoming.Frequency.bif_le`, `Becoming.Frequency.count_le_succ`, `Becoming.Frequency.count_mono`, `Becoming.Frequency.count_le`, `Becoming.Frequency.marked_between`, `Becoming.Frequency.recurs_of_unbounded`)
2. With the part giving no gap after the start, starting gaps at most D, and the strengths into each condition at most M at each step and zero at unmarked steps, the carried amount is at most D·(1 + M)^a, a the marked steps before; where 2^a is at most A·(t + 1)^n it is at most D·A^M·(t + 1)^(nM). With every condition listed, the steps at which anything couples are such a schedule. (`Becoming.Frequency.step_eq`, `Becoming.Frequency.succ_le_two_pow`, `Becoming.Frequency.pow_le_two_pow_pow`, `Becoming.inflow_congr_strength`, `Becoming.carried_le_count`, `Becoming.carried_le_of_rare`, `Becoming.Frequency.coupling`, `Becoming.Frequency.quiet_coupling`, `Becoming.carried_le_coupling`)
3. A condition returning its level to itself with strength M at a schedule's marked steps couples exactly there, each coupling a return, recurs where marked steps come as late as one likes, and carries exactly D·(1 + M)^a; with positive strength and start, it is bounded by a polynomial exactly where 2^a is, whatever the strength. (`Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.strengths`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.strengths_on`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.strengths_off`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.give`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.inflow_eq`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.into`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.quiet`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.carried_eq`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.polynomial_iff`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.couplesAt`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.recurs`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.returns`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.couplesAt_iff`)
4. A coupling reading d's level at step s into c adds at least what had reached d by s. A chain in time order carries what reached its start to its end; one back to where it began is a return, and each return at least doubles what had reached it, R returns by 2^R; where something arrived and returns come at steps T i with 2^i outgrowing every polynomial in T i, no polynomial bounds it, whatever the strengths. (`Becoming.carried_step_ge_at`, `Becoming.ChainInTime`, `Becoming.ChainInTime.start_le`, `Becoming.carried_along_in_time`, `Becoming.Returns`, `Becoming.Returns.of_couplesAt`, `Becoming.carried_doubles_return`, `Becoming.carried_returns`, `Becoming.runaway_of_returns`)
5. The sparse schedule marks 0, 1, 3, 7, …: with c steps marked before t, t + 1 ≤ 2^c ≤ 2t + 1, so 2^a ≤ 2(t + 1), and its count is unbounded. The self-loop coupling there with positive strength recurs, so from a positive start every finite order misses something, yet it carries at most D·2^M·(t + 1)^M. (`Becoming.Frequency.Sparse.marks`, `Becoming.Frequency.Sparse.on`, `Becoming.Frequency.Sparse.count_eq`, `Becoming.Frequency.Sparse.bounds`, `Becoming.Frequency.Sparse.double_eq`, `Becoming.Frequency.Sparse.rare`, `Becoming.Frequency.Sparse.unbounded`, `Becoming.Frequency.Sparse.often`, `Becoming.Frequency.Sparse.recurs`, `Becoming.Frequency.Sparse.inexact`, `Becoming.Frequency.Sparse.polynomial`)
6. A coupling stops by N where none of its couplings reads a level from N on: one that stops does not recur, and stops by every later step. With every condition listed, where each pair's coupling recurs or stops by some step, the schedule has settled by some step, the finitely many bounds added. (`Becoming.StopsBy`, `Becoming.StopsBy.mono`, `Becoming.StopsBy.not_recurs`, `Becoming.Frequency.bound_list`, `Becoming.settled_of_each`)
7. Whether a coupling at step m reads a level from step n on is decided. The dichotomy that every decided two-place family has every row true somewhere or some row false throughout gives the limited principle of omniscience; given it, with every condition listed each coupling recurs or stops, and every schedule settles. (`Becoming.Frequency.readsLate`, `Becoming.Frequency.readsLate_of_couplesAt`, `Becoming.Frequency.couplesAt_of_readsLate`, `Becoming.RecursOrStops`, `Becoming.RecursOrStops.lpo`, `Becoming.recurs_or_stops`, `Becoming.settled_of_recursOrStops`)
8. The self-loop coupling at the first step at which a decided sequence q is true couples at most once and does not recur; where it settles, q is true somewhere or false throughout. So that these schedules, each coupling at most once, all settle gives the limited principle of omniscience. (`Becoming.Frequency.First.strengths`, `Becoming.Frequency.First.of_couplesAt`, `Becoming.Frequency.First.couplesAt_first`, `Becoming.Frequency.First.once`, `Becoming.Frequency.First.not_recurs`, `Becoming.Frequency.First.decides`, `Becoming.lpo_of_settled`)
9. The self-loop reading level s once every row up to s has been true somewhere recurs exactly where every row is; where it settles, the limited principle of omniscience decides the rows up to its settling step, and the dichotomy follows. So every schedule of one condition returning to itself settling, and every schedule of every world with its conditions listed settling, are each exactly the dichotomy. (`Becoming.Frequency.Rows.or_cases`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.or_left`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.or_right`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.anyUpTo`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.allUpTo`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.anyUpTo_of`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.anyUpTo_true`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.allUpTo_true`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.allUpTo_of`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.found`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.strengths`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.found_of_couplesAt`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.couplesAt_of_found`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.witnessed`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.couplesAt_of_rows`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.recurs_iff`, `Becoming.Frequency.Rows.decide_rows`, `Becoming.settled_iff_recursOrStops`, `Becoming.settled_every_iff`)
10. The self-loop of Becoming.Loops couples at every step and carries D·(1 + M)^t; the loop of Becoming.Closing forming at T couples at every step from T and carries D·2^r at T + r. Through gap_le_carried the rate bounds every gap between two balanced flows of every law with the strengths. (`Becoming.Frequency.count_always`, `Becoming.Frequency.count_before`, `Becoming.Frequency.count_from`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.always`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.always_carried`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.onset`, `Becoming.Frequency.SelfLoop.onset_amount`, `Becoming.gap_le_count`)
11. In a world: the world of a self-loop of strength M coupling at the steps a schedule marks, from a gap D, balances and stands at D·(1 + M)^a, a the marked steps so far; with M and D at least one its standing is polynomially bounded exactly where 2^a is; on the sparse schedule, M and D positive, its coupling recurs, its standing is at most D·2^M·(t + 1)^M, and no finite order of the carried amount is exact. (`Becoming.FormedLoops.scheduleWorld`, `Becoming.FormedLoops.scheduleWorld_course`, `Becoming.FormedLoops.sparseWorld_course`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom. The coupling strengths k are supplied bounds and the schedule on a supplied decided sequence; the list of conditions is arbitrary, every condition being listed only where a theorem writes every.
- In the rate, the part giving no gap after the start, starting gaps at most D, and the strengths into each condition at most M at each step and zero at unmarked steps; the dichotomy RecursOrStops, where used, is written in as a hypothesis, never assumed, and so are settled schedules.
- In the rate for every law (gap_le_count), every condition listed, with decided equality of conditions used only in its proof, through gap_le_carried.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That every schedule settles: it is exactly RecursOrStops, which gives the limited principle of omniscience; reading it as Σ⁰₂ excluded middle (Akama, Berardi, Hayashi and Kohlenbach 2004) is cited, not proved in Lean.
- A loop of recurring couplings upstream does not imply runaway: the sparse self-loop recurs, yet its carried amount is bounded by a polynomial. Witness: `Becoming.Frequency.Sparse.polynomial`.
- Whether, beyond the self-loop, the most difference that can arrive meets the bound by returns or the bound by coupling steps; the spectral radius of given strengths.
- Real amounts, where a positive strength may be below one and shrinking strengths could keep frequent returns from running away; how often a given law's couplings act; continuous time.
- **Counterexample:** The sparse self-loop: one condition returning its level to itself at steps 0, 1, 3, 7, …; its coupling recurs and every finite order misses something, yet the carried amount is at most D·2^M·(t + 1)^M: a loop of recurring couplings need not run away. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Frequency.lean)
- **Counterexample:** The self-loop at the first true step: it couples at the step a decided sequence is first true, at most once; that all these schedules settle gives the limited principle of omniscience: every schedule settling is at least as strong as that principle. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Frequency.lean)

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Ren, 12 October 2026, on the loops: “how how accurate can we do that uh what is the limitation do we have losses”, with the goal “move towards 100%”; on 16 October Ren called the AI's reading of “only a loop makes a difference run away” right (“your read on this is right”), a reading that left couplings at only some steps open. This result answers the first two items of what-a-cut-loses' next_delta. Readings (the AI's, taken by Ren on 18 October 2026, DELEGATED-CHOICES D43): how fast a difference runs away is set by how often couplings act: frequent returns make it run away (with natural-number strengths, each positive one at least one; with strengths below one this need not follow) and rare coupling steps keep it polynomial whatever the strengths, strength changing only how large; for a self-loop how often it couples decides exactly. Couplings at only some steps are closed both ways: only a loop of the couplings that go on can make it run away, and such a loop need not. That every schedule settles is a principle of reasoning, not a fact the theory asserts or denies of the unfolding. The mathematics is standard: a discrete Grönwall bound counting only the steps that act, doubling at each return, and a Σ⁰₂ form of excluded middle.
